solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the drink's letters stand around the fault

parts.note: nog is a drink, as in eggnog
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: Someone tests whether a drink is free of defects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking about inquisitively, as in nosing around, is a way of prying into or inspecting things.

parts.note: never can be put as not, as in 'not ever'
Aries is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A slogan refusing to give homes to bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a zodiac house, the first sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are legal functionaries who witness and certify documents, a kind of public official.

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters of the words turn into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's oldest child withdraws from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered life is a protected, withdrawn one, close in sense to a hermit-like existence.

clue.text: Man finds fool's gold in the Bahamas

parts.note: a man is a chess piece, and N is the notation for the knight
an ass is a fool
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A man strikes iron pyrites while in the Caribbean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool's gold' wants to be pyrites, but it is two pieces. Reading 'Man' as a chess man, the knight, is a stretch, though it is what gives the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas, so it is a place found there.

definitions.meaning: physical meeting of two things, being in touch

explanation.definitionFit: A moving scene is described as affecting, and things that meet physically are said to be in contact.

clue.text: Arrangement for lecture about royal casket

indicators.note: about means the lecture's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech or lecture
a casket is a small chest

explanation.surface: Plans for a talk about a regal coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the casket and royal pieces inside the lecture, with the casket going in first, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestration is the scoring of music for an ensemble, and more broadly any careful organising of events.

clue.text: Depression settled on one reclining manual worker

indicators.note: settled on places the depression ahead of the next piece, sitting on it in the down entry

parts.note: a col is a dip between two mountain peaks
a lier is one who lies down

explanation.surface: A worn-out labourer slumps in a hollow, lying back.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a classic example of a labourer working with their hands.

indicators.note: accommodation suggests adjusting or fitting the letters into a new layout

explanation.surface: Someone renting lodgings in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which makes the capitalised word look like a place; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to put a body in a grave, the burial sense of the verb.

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spicy fish dish that has no flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tasteless' looks like bland food but means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showy and vulgar is lacking in good taste, the aesthetic rather than culinary sense.

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, here losing its first letter

parts.note: to stress something is to emphasise it

explanation.surface: An instruction to highlight a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock or long strand of hair on the head.

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a bear is a stock-market speculator who sells expecting a fall

explanation.surface: A headless bear turns out to be a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the stock-exchange sense, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator embezzles funds entrusted to them, a form of stealing.

definitions.meaning: an 'ordinary' is the old name for the high-wheeled bicycle
two copper coins of old British money, a penny and a farthing (a quarter of a penny)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary coppers' reads as regular police; the farthing was a pre-decimal British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian big-wheeled bicycle was nicknamed after two coins of different sizes, and was called an ordinary in its day.

clue.text: Check if son is off school again

indicators.note: is off means the son's letter leaves the word for check

parts.note: to restrain is to check or hold back
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A parent asks whether their boy is skipping lessons once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train, so teaching someone a fresh set of skills is training them again.

indicators.note: maltreated suggests the word is roughly handled and its letters knocked about

explanation.surface: People who have fled abused by governments.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are people who left their country, often for political reasons, as exiles.

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Picking up a little knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain money or reward through work is to obtain it.

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed and changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A nervous condition has received therapy in the past twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria was classically regarded as a psychological disorder of uncontrolled emotion.

parts.note: the hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle, so it is a long side

explanation.surface: A geometry query about whether a line is an edge of a shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'a hypotenuse' is described by a phrase rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying next to and parallel with something is to be beside it, at its edge.

parts.note: a batsman in cricket who is batting is said to be in
a stance is a way of standing, a position

explanation.surface: Describing a batter's posture as a sample case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' for batting is cricket usage: the batting side is 'in'. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, as in 'for instance'.

clue.text: Settlement of conflict is in hand

indicators.note: is in places the conflict inside the word for hand

parts.note: a deal is the hand of cards dealt to a player
a fray is a fight or conflict

explanation.surface: Resolving a dispute is something being handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hand' reads as an idiom meaning under control; here it is the container. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Defraying costs means paying them, so the noun is the payment or settling of a bill.

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: in places the workers inside the abbreviation for right

parts.note: men are workers, as in a firm's staff

explanation.surface: Steelworkers getting themselves in a proper state.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferment is a state of agitation or excitement, a flap or fuss.

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The lowest position overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low point' looks like a single phrase meaning a nadir; it is a cow's sound plus a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is the most obvious body seen up above at night, so it sits overhead.

indicators.note: enter means the student goes inside the word for lido

parts.note: a lido is a bathing place, likened to a beach
L, from the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Telling a learner to go swimming and lose their colour.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an open-air public swimming pool or bathing beach, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach something is to whiten it by removing colour.

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the beast above the trouble

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An animal attacks once the difficulty is past.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone is to attack them, which is what assailing means.

indicators.note: outside means the allowed word stands around the always word

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A child who has permanent permission to play outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, a youngster in the animal world.

clue.text: See number one vehicle for clergyman

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see, used in references
I is the Roman numeral for one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bishop's see sends its top car for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a bishop's diocese, apt beside clergyman, but it is the reference abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England parish priest, one kind of clergyman.

clue.text: The perception to manufacture this gin

indicators.note: to manufacture means making something new out of the material, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A distiller's knack for producing this spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is the ability to see clearly into a situation, a deep understanding or discernment.

indicators.note: during places the corps and soldiers inside the word for battle

parts.note: action is military combat
C is an abbreviation for corps
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common stand-in for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops being gathered up in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretion is the gradual gathering or building up of material, a process of accumulating.

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means belonging to another country or strange, like foreign.

indicators.note: loses means the Frenchman's letter is taken away from the gallery

parts.note: the Hermitage is the great art museum in St Petersburg
M, for monsieur, stands for a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A museum in St Petersburg is denied a Frenchman's legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, an inheritance or legacy.

parts.note: to flee is to run away fast
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A con artist cheats then hurries out of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, as a sheep is shorn.
